## Design note

The quiet assassin. Heaviest of the supercars and the least powerful on paper, but the electric torque hits from walking pace and the front motors pull it out of corners, so it is the easiest supercar to drive fast and the best in the wet. It runs out of breath on a long highway against the V8 and V12. The nine-speed gearbox never leaves it off-boost.

## How this car breaks

Aluminium spaceframe with a carbon floor and composite panels. The traction battery in the tunnel is protected by the sills; side hits that reach it count as fuel-tank damage. The V6, motor and gearbox live on the rear subframe (rear hits kill drive) and the front motors share the nose with the radiators, so a firm frontal costs drive too.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

|---|---|---|---|
| roll | 799 | 0.78 | 620 |
| pitch | 3303 | 0.76 | 2510 |
| yaw | 3654 | 0.76 | 2780 |

## Aerodynamics

Frontal area A = 0.83·W·H = 1.95 m²; Cd = 0.34 → **CdA = 0.662 m²**. Lift Cl·A front/rear = -0.05 / -0.12 m² (class-typical; positive = lift). No add-on aero (`aero_downforce_coeffs` = 0, mods add it).

## Engine

3.5 L DOHC 24-valve 75° V6, twin turbos, dry sump, plus a direct-drive motor between engine and gearbox; curve is the combined crank-equivalent output. Class-typical 2010s hybrid supercar: 3.5 TT V6 (~370 kW) plus ~110 kW of electric assist, ~418 kW combined at 7000 rpm, 646 N·m from 2500. Electric torque fills the bottom end before the turbos spool, so the curve is nearly flat from 1500 — no turbo lag. The front-axle motors are folded into the fixed AWD split.

## Drivetrain

9-speed dual-clutch, through-the-road hybrid AWD (twin front motors modelled as a fixed 35 % front split with a mild front LSD for their torque vectoring), clutch-type rear LSD. Layout **AWD, 35 % front**; front diff: clutch LSD, preload 30 N·m, power ramp 0.30, coast ramp 0.10; rear diff: clutch LSD, preload 50 N·m, power ramp 0.40, coast ramp 0.25. Clutch capacity 1.45 × peak torque = 940 N·m. Shift time 0.18 s.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.30 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 363 kg | 1.85 Hz | 49000 N/m | 2530 N·s/m | 3800 N·s/m | 0.12 m |
| Rear | 508 kg | 2.05 Hz | 84200 N/m | 3920 N·s/m | 5880 N·s/m | 0.13 m |

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 1.6°/g with 53% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.307 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 197558 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 67972 F / 111870 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **13300 F / 0 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 1.5°/g, front share 48%. Bump stops 200000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -1.2° F / -1.6° R, toe +0.00° F / +0.20° R (+ = in), caster 7.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 390 mm disc, pistons per side 38 mm + 36 mm + 34 mm → A = 30.6 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 170 mm, pad μ = 0.45: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.45·100 bar·30.6 cm²·0.170 m = **4682 N·m**
- Rear: 360 mm disc, pistons per side 36 mm + 32 mm → A = 18.2 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 155 mm, pad μ = 0.43: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.43·100 bar·18.2 cm²·0.155 m = **2429 N·m**

ABS ceiling: caliper capacity 4682 / 2429 N·m exceeds 1.5 × the front lock torque on this car's tire (peak μ 1.20), which `wp_vehicle`'s ABS cannot modulate (it releases to a fraction of the commanded torque, so an oversized caliper keeps the wheel locked). Both axles scaled by 0.63 → **2960 / 1530 N·m**. Remove when 02's ABS modulates relative to lock torque.

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 1643 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.80×), rear needs 1267 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.21×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 2283 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity is below that (hardware-limited rear), so `bias_front` = **0.5**: both axles get full caliper torque → delivered 2960 N·m front / 1530 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 2600 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 14.0:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 11.8 m → outer-front path radius 5.78 m, rear-axle-centre radius 4.31 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.548 rad (31.4°)** (outer 27.1°, inner 37.1° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.50). Rack speed 1.7 rad/s.

## Damage lattice (`data/lattices/kagero_hx.json`)

276 nodes, 1772 beams, 6 detachables, 21 component mounts.

- Generated with `gen-lattice --id kagero_hx --profile coupe --width 1.94 --length 4.49 --height 1.21 --wheelbase 2.63 --mass 366.6 --car-mass 1833.0 --clearance 0.11 --front-overhang 0.98 --strength 1.0` (20% of vehicle mass in the lattice; strength from durability class 3).
- Era `2010s`: gen-lattice's default HSS passenger cell kept as is.
- Aluminium body: 610 outer-panel beams mild_steel → aluminum.
- Mid-engine: engine block moved behind the cabin bulkhead (y -0.85…-1.50 m), mounted to the rear rails and the bulkhead; 10 nodes behind the bulkhead relabelled FrameRear (engine bay, not cabin); 16 front-rail beams × 1.6 (no engine block in the nose: they get gen-lattice's rear-rail factor); 166 rear-subframe beams → aluminum ×1.5 section (sacrificial); gearbox and half-shafts at the rear axle, side fuel tanks at the sills behind the seats; engine fails at 0.12 m, gearbox 0.08 m.
